meta.title: Who really said "The great gift of human beings is that we have the power of empathy"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes, Meryl Streep — a curated reference traces it to a 1991 Cosmopolitan interview, but the popular one-liner truncates a longer remark about her acting process.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The great gift of human beings is that we have the power of empathy'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuinely Meryl Streep, and consistent with her lifelong view of empathy as the actor's art — but the viral one-liner is a truncated, source-stripped fragment of a longer 1991 interview quote.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Widely and consistently credited to Meryl Streep, and consistent with her lifelong framing of empathy as the heart of acting. A curated empathy-quotes reference traces it to a May 1991 Cosmopolitan interview with Michael Segell, where it appears in fuller form — but the primary magazine could not be independently examined, so we mark it attributed rather than verified.

source.heading: Where the line comes from

docMeta.dd: ‘Culture of Empathy’ reference, citing Cosmopolitan, May 1991 (interview by Michael Segell)
On why she is drawn to play so many different women
Circulates as a source-free one-liner; the fuller wording is documented

source.excerpt: The great gift of human beings is that we have the power of empathy, we can all sense a mysterious connection to each other. I like to investigate these different women to see what the commonality is with me. When I get the script and read their story, I hear the ‘ping!’ that makes a connection with my own life.
trail: A curated empathy-quotes reference records the line under “1991-05 — Cosmo,” as Streep speaking to Michael Segell, and preserves the fuller “‘ping!’” continuation (Culture of Empathy).
On Goodreads the fuller “mysterious connection” wording appears, attributed to Streep with the standard disclaimer that community quotes are “not verified.”
The theme is unmistakably hers: in her 2010 Barnard commencement address she calls empathy “the heart of the actor’s art” — but that speech does not contain this exact line.
source.excerptNote: The viral quote stops at “…connection to each other.” The rest shows it was a remark about Streep’s acting process, not a free-standing aphorism.

source.rightsNote: The words are Streep’s, documented in a 1991 Cosmopolitan interview — well after 1931 — so the remark is in copyright as her spoken statement within a copyrighted magazine interview. Rights rest with Streep as speaker and Hearst as publisher of the interview.

author.name: Meryl Streep
author.heading: Meryl Streep
author.bio: Meryl Streep (b. 1949) is among the most acclaimed screen actors in history, a record-holder for Academy Award nominations. She has returned again and again to empathy as the core of her craft — telling Barnard’s 2010 graduates that “empathy is at the heart of the actor’s art,” which makes this remark about the “power of empathy” entirely in character.

misattribution.heading: The catch: it’s real, but truncated
misattribution.intro: Unlike most quotes pinned on famous names, this one does appear to be genuinely Streep’s. The problem is how it travels: stripped of any source and cut off mid-thought.

items.why: Quote sites end it at “…the power of empathy” or “…connection to each other,” turning a working actor’s comment about choosing roles into a stand-alone inspirational slogan. The documented remark continues into the “‘ping!’” she feels reading a script (Culture of Empathy).
Goodreads, Good News Network and others print the line with no date, publication or interviewer — which is why it is often mistaken for a line from a speech she never used it in.
Because that address made empathy famous as her theme, the quote is sometimes assumed to come from it. It does not: the full transcript contains no such line.

misattribution.truthLine: The thought is authentically Streep’s — documented in a 1991 Cosmopolitan interview — but the internet’s version is a source-free half of a longer sentence about her acting process.

context.heading: Why the line rings true
lead: Streep has spent decades describing acting as an act of empathy rather than imitation. In the 1991 remark the phrase belongs to a practical thought: she is explaining that she seeks out very different women because she can sense a “commonality” with each — the “ping” of recognition when she reads a script.

That is why the quote survives detached from its source: it distills a genuine, repeated conviction. Nearly two decades later she told Barnard’s graduating class that “empathy is at the heart of the actor’s art,” the same idea in different words.
context.pull: Empathy is at the heart of the actor’s art. — Streep, Barnard, 2010
